modelReview.summary: The study lacks fundamental methodological rigor: no proportional hazards assumption testing, no confounder selection rationale or adjustment for measured confounders beyond age/severity, missing variable definitions, no descriptive statistics, and insufficient model diagnostics. These issues render results uninterpretable and require substantial revision before the manuscript can be considered for promotion.

findings.title: Missing proportional hazards assumption testing
findings.whyItMatters: Cox regression requires the proportional hazards assumption to produce valid hazard ratios. Without formal testing (e.g., Schoenfeld residuals, log-log plots), the reported treatment effect may be invalid or misleading.
findings.actionableFix: Compute Schoenfeld residuals and report a global test for each covariate and overall. Provide scaled Schoenfeld residual plots or a log-log survival plot to assess proportionality.
findings.deterministicVerification: Check diagnostics.json for presence of 'proportional_hazards_tests' or similar field with p-values.

findings.title: Variable definitions and coding are missing
findings.whyItMatters: Interpretation of hazard ratios depends entirely on variable coding: whether treatment is binary, how aging is scaled (per year, per decade), whether severity is continuous or categorical, and what event/survival_time represent. Without definitions, the numeric results are meaningless.
findings.actionableFix: Provide explicit definitions for every variable: measurement unit, category labels, reference group if applicable, and data source. For continuous variables, state the unit of increment corresponding to the HR.

findings.title: Insufficient adjustment for confounding
findings.whyItMatters: Observational studies require a plausible confounder selection strategy (e.g., DAG, literature-based) to reduce bias. Using only age and severity likely leaves substantial residual confounding, making the association between treatment and outcome unreliable.
findings.actionableFix: Develop a causal diagram, identify a minimally sufficient adjustment set, and either include those variables in a multivariable model or use propensity score methods. Provide a sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding.

findings.title: Missing data handling not described
findings.whyItMatters: Complete-case analysis (n=240) can introduce selection bias if missingness is related to exposure, outcome, or covariates. Without reporting the amount and pattern of missingness, readers cannot assess potential bias.
findings.actionableFix: Report missingness proportions per variable, compare characteristics of excluded vs. included subjects, and consider multiple imputation or a sensitivity analysis (e.g., pattern-mixture model).

findings.title: Lack of descriptive statistics
findings.whyItMatters: Without a baseline characteristics table (Table 1), it is impossible to assess comparability of treatment groups, potential confounding, or generalizability of the sample.
findings.actionableFix: Include a table summarizing demographic and clinical features by treatment arm, with appropriate statistical comparisons (standardized differences preferred over p-values).

findings.title: Insufficient model diagnostics beyond event count
findings.whyItMatters: The only diagnostic provided is number of events (140) and predictors (3). Model fit, influential observations, or assumption checks (linearity, additivity) are absent, undermining trust in the estimates.
findings.actionableFix: Report model fit statistics (e.g., concordance, R²), check for non-linearity (martingale residuals), and assess influential points (dfbetas).

findings.title: Data and analysis code not provided
findings.whyItMatters: Although artifacts are listed, the raw data and the execution scripts are not available, limiting full reproducibility.
findings.actionableFix: Include a de-identified version of the dataset and all analysis scripts in a public repository (e.g., OSF, GitHub) or state why this is not possible.

findings.title: Overly defensive claims border on meta-commentary
findings.whyItMatters: Phrases like 'methods review is required before stronger claims' and 'this report is bound to the artifacts...' are unusual in a scientific manuscript and may undermine reader confidence.
findings.actionableFix: Phrase limitations in standard scientific language (e.g., 'This study is observational and cannot prove causality; results may not generalize beyond the study population.') without referencing the review process itself.

missingEvidence: Variable codebook with units and coding
Descriptive statistics table (baseline characteristics by treatment group)
Confounder selection rationale (DAG or causal model)
Model fit statistics (concordance, likelihood ratio test)
Raw dataset or analysis scripts for reproducibility
